content.text:
Start the dev server with `npm run dev`. The URLs below assume Rsbuild's default address, `http://localhost:3000`; I couldn't find the project's dev-server config, so use whatever address `npm run dev` prints. I used `map=jackie` because it has the most tree cover; `map=ajvatovci` also works. Put the stage in the URL (`map=…`) so the game skips the menu and the extra parameters aren't lost.

**1. Benchmark: how much the trees cost**
```
http://localhost:3000/games/rally/?map=jackie&quality=medium&treebench=1
```
- Leave the tab in front and don't touch anything. The camera flies a fixed 1,200-frame path twice, once with trees and once without, and each pass is preceded by a warm-up.
- When it finishes, a JSON report downloads. The browser console also prints `tree cost X ms / frame`, which is the trees' own cost.
- The spec's budget is at most 1 ms added to the average frame and to the 1% low. Anything over that is marked as a failure in the report.

**2. The same benchmark with the depth prepass on**
```
http://localhost:3000/games/rally/?map=jackie&quality=medium&treebench=1&treeprepass=1
```
- Compare its tree cost with run 1. If it is much lower, overdraw (sprites shaded several times per pixel) is the main problem.

**3. Live stats while driving**
```
http://localhost:3000/games/rally/?map=jackie&quality=medium&treedebug=1
```
- This tints trees by detail level and shows the stats overlay at top left: trees per level, sprite count, and draw calls, triangles and GPU time for the main and shadow passes.
- Drive into dense forest and watch whether the main pass or the shadow pass has the larger GPU time.

**4. Checking the prepass for depth errors**
```
http://localhost:3000/games/rally/?map=jackie&quality=medium&treeprepass=1&treedebug=5
```
- Look for magenta pixels in tree crowns. They mean the two passes disagreed on depth on your GPU, so the prepass isn't safe to turn on by default there.

Use the same quality and window size for every run, or the results can't be compared. Send me the two JSON reports, or paste the overlay numbers from run 3, and I'll tell you which fix will gain the most.
